import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.59

by V. P. Shunkov

A group is biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup $H$, any two elements of
prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. It is conjugacy biprimitively finite
if this condition is required only when the two elements are conjugate. The problem asks
whether periodic groups of finite rank satisfying either condition are locally finite, and
also records the corresponding special cases for groups without involutions.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 6.59.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.59»

/-- A group is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Group.FG H → Finite H

/-- A group has finite (special, or Prüfer) rank if there is a uniform finite bound on the
number of generators needed for each of its finitely generated subgroups. -/
def IsFiniteRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ H : Subgroup G, Group.FG H →
    ∃ S : Finset H, S.card ≤ r ∧ Subgroup.closure (S : Set H) = ⊤

/-- A group $G$ is biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    letI : (H.subgroupOf H.normalizer).Normal :=
      Subgroup.normal_subgroupOf_of_le_normalizer le_rfl
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is conjugacy biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup $H \le G$,
any two conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    letI : (H.subgroupOf H.normalizer).Normal :=
      Subgroup.normal_subgroupOf_of_le_normalizer le_rfl
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      IsConj x y → (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime →
        Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/--
Prove that every periodic biprimitively finite group of finite (special, or Prüfer) rank is
locally finite. Here periodic means that every element has finite order; the two elements
of prime order in each normalizer quotient may have different prime orders.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.59» :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G → IsBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      IsFiniteRank G → IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

/--
Prove that every periodic conjugacy biprimitively finite group of finite (special, or
Prüfer) rank is locally finite. Thus the finiteness condition in each $N_G(H)/H$ is assumed
only for pairs of conjugate prime-order elements.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.59».variants.conjugacy :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G → IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      IsFiniteRank G → IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

/--
Prove, in particular, that every periodic biprimitively finite group of finite (special, or
Prüfer) rank having no involutions is locally finite. Having no involutions means that no
element has order $2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.59».variants.no_involutions :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G → IsBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      IsFiniteRank G → (∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ 2) → IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

/--
Prove that every periodic conjugacy biprimitively finite group of finite (special, or
Prüfer) rank having no involutions is locally finite. This combines the conjugacy and
no-involutions variants: in each $N_G(H)/H$, only conjugate prime-order pairs are subject
to the finiteness condition, and no element of $G$ has order $2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.59».variants.conjugacy_no_involutions :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G → IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      IsFiniteRank G → (∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ 2) → IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.59»

not used in its claim.

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

def IsLocallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- A group has *finite rank* (special rank in the sense of Mal'cev, also called Prüfer rank)
if there is an $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated
by at most $r$ elements. -/
def HasFiniteRank : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r

prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. The two primes may differ, and $H$ may

  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →

    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})
